issue.description:
Publishing is automatic since R026, but assembling the git commit is still manual and is a reliable footgun. Two ways it goes wrong, both hit on 2026-09-02:

1. 'git commit <paths>' stages tracked modifications but NOT new untracked files. Committing .beads/checkpoint by pathspec silently omitted a freshly written object, and NEEDLE's checkpoint-verification hook rejected it:
     checkpoint-publish: error: staged current.json root is missing from the index:
     objects/0a82a10efc9dcd70eb7e89305809130356e101910f6d6bfd114b7a1fc257c66e.jsonl
   Without that hook the commit would have recorded a checkpoint referencing an object that was not in the tree.

2. Compaction renames objects, so a hand-written pathspec is stale the moment it is typed. In one commit the same operation appeared as two R099 renames plus an untracked directory.

bead-rs already computes the exact consistent set -- sync status names the verified root. Have it stage that set after a successful publish. Staging is idempotent, mutates no history, needs no branch policy, and removes this entire error class; whoever commits next picks up a correct fileset.

Deliberately NOT committing -- see the auto-commit bead for why that is the wrong layer.

The obvious objection is polluting a concurrent worker's index on a shared checkout. It inverts here: checkpoint files are shared state that is supposed to be committed, so being swept into another worker's commit is the correct outcome for them, unlike a source file being swept (which is the real hazard, and is a separate concern).
issue.title: Stage the verified checkpoint fileset automatically after publishing it

issue.description:
## Incident

During the 2026-09-03 NEEDLE fleet run, multiple workers appeared to claim the same bead. The claim transaction itself remained serialized; duplication became possible after a live claimant was reaped and the same issue was legally claimed again, while the original agent process kept running.

Concrete sequence from `/home/coding/spaxel` for `spaxel-97b27661`:

1. `glm-face` claimed at 2026-09-03T02:57:58Z.
2. Another NEEDLE worker's Mend pass released that claim at 03:03:03Z as age 305s, even though `glm-face` still had fresh process/worker heartbeats and its agent ran until 03:20:18Z.
3. `glm-spaxel` claimed at 03:10:48Z, was similarly released at 03:15:53Z, and `glm-spaxel2` claimed at 03:16:56Z.
4. The stale `glm-face` execution then closed the bead at 03:18:10Z while the newer `glm-spaxel2` claim epoch was active.

The same five-minute stale release pattern was observed on `spaxel-5b98e686` and `seam-2bf38c53`. NEEDLE also failed open when its post-claim `show` used the wrong/home store for a remote-workspace bead (`Issue not found`, then "proceeding with dispatch"), which amplifies the incident but does not explain the store-level stale mutation.

## Problem

`bead claim` atomically selects and assigns one ready issue, but an ordinary non-leased claim does not give the claimant a mandatory epoch credential. `bead close`, `bead release`, and `bead update` accept optional `--if-revision`/`--fencing-token`; callers that omit them can mutate whatever claim epoch is current. After release/reclaim, a stale process can therefore close, release, or overwrite a newer worker's claim.

This defeats the safety boundary expected from atomic claims: single-winner claim selection is insufficient unless later lifecycle mutations are fenced to that winner's claim epoch.

Related existing work: `beadrs-33fcfa12` (atomic attempt resolution), `beadrs-541da6de` (atomic revision guards), `beadrs-8afb1ba3` and `beadrs-e2dbc36f` (concurrency suites). None currently captures this live claimant -> external release -> new claimant -> stale claimant mutation sequence.

## Investigation and fix

Determine and document the native contract for claimant-owned lifecycle mutations after reassignment. Implement a backward-compatible mechanism that lets automated consumers prove they still own the current claim epoch and makes a stale claimant fail with conflict/exit 4 without changing the newer claim.

Evaluate claim revision, lease fencing token, an explicit claim-epoch token, and the atomic `resolve` path. Keep operator/admin recovery possible only through an explicit, auditable path; do not silently weaken stale-owner protection for automation compatibility.

Record the corresponding NEEDLE consumer requirements in the compatibility spec: retain the claim revision/token, use it for completion/release/update/resolve, and fail closed when live-store claim verification cannot be performed. The NEEDLE five-minute false-reap policy itself is consumer-side follow-up, but bead-rs must contain the damage from any mistaken release/reclaim.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a deterministic two-process/two-connection regression test: worker A claims; a reaper releases; worker B claims; stale A attempts close, release, update, and attempt resolution. Every stale operation conflicts atomically and B remains `in_progress` and assigned.
- A correctly fenced mutation from worker B succeeds, including the selected `resolve` path.
- Simultaneous claim tests still prove exactly one claimant wins an initially ready bead.
- Protection works for ordinary non-leased claims as well as leased claims; historical lease rows do not brick a later valid epoch.
- Missing or stale epoch/revision credentials have an explicit documented compatibility result. Automated-consumer APIs must not silently mutate a newer claim epoch.
- Admin recovery/override, if retained, is explicit and audit-visible.
- Audit events, change feed, resource locks, and checkpoint publication remain transactionally consistent on both conflict and success.
- Update `research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md`, command help/capabilities/schema as applicable, and add an installed-CLI integration fixture reproducing the incident sequence.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` pass, including repeated concurrency/stress execution.
issue.title: Fence stale claimants from mutating a newer claim epoch

issue.close_reason: Fixed in 9ed0123 (pushed to origin/main). Chose option 3 - treat expired/foreign lease rows as absent when the current claim was non-leased - implemented as claim-epoch scoping in validate_lease_for_mutation: when no ACTIVE lease matches the current assignee, the historical row only fences if it belongs to the current assignee AND the most recent 'claimed' event records a leased claim (with_lease:true; events.sequence is monotonic so no timestamp comparison). Rejected purge-on-release/close: leases.issue_id is the PRIMARY KEY, so the single row IS the per-issue fencing-token high-water mark (MAX(fencing_token)) - purging would reset tokens and break the monotonicity R002 documents. Verified live: the scripted repro (leased claim w1 -> release -> plain claim w2 -> close) now exits 0; expired lease of the CURRENT leased epoch still refuses with exit 4 (fencing unchanged); same-name plain re-claim also survives old-lease expiry. tests/r002_leased_claims.rs: new test_plain_reclaim_after_leased_release_is_mutable + all 10 originals pass; full cargo test 712 passed / 0 failed. Out-of-scope findings while investigating: (1) 'claim --fencing-token' on an issue that already has a lease row fails with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: leases.issue_id' (create_lease INSERTs rather than replacing - latent pre-existing bug); (2) an issue whose CURRENT leased epoch has expired remains unreleasable/unclosable with no operator override - pre-existing R002 stale-worker fencing semantics, unchanged here.
issue.description:
src/service/leases.rs:248-303 (validate_lease_for_mutation): when no ACTIVE lease matches (issue, current assignee), the mere existence of ANY historical lease row (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leases WHERE issue_id = ?) raises Error::LeaseExpired. Lease rows are never deleted: release_issue_impl/close_issue_impl (src/service/lifecycle.rs:344-436) do not purge them and cleanup_expired_leases (leases.rs:342) is #[allow(dead_code)], never called. All four lifecycle ops call validate_lease_for_mutation whenever the issue has an assignee (lifecycle.rs:47,102,142,176).

Net effect: once an issue has EVER been claimed with --lease-ttl, any later NON-leased claimant is permanently locked out of close/release/update — the issue is stuck in_progress+assigned forever (the classic fleet-starvation shape) with no CLI recovery path (update --clear-assignee hits the same validation).

Reproduced live at HEAD (dac3910): 'bead claim --assignee w1 --lease-ttl 30' -> 'bead release <id>' -> 'bead claim --assignee w2' (plain) -> 'bead close <id> --reason done' fails exit 4 'Lease for issue ... has expired or is invalid for assignee w2'; release and update fail identically.

Fix options (pick one, document in the close reason): purge the issue's lease rows on release/close; or scope the 'lease existed' check to the current assignment epoch (e.g. leases created at/after the current claim event); or treat expired/foreign lease rows as absent when the current claim was non-leased.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Script the repro above in a temp workspace; w2's close now succeeds exit 0.
2. Active-holder fencing is unchanged: existing tests/r002_leased_claims.rs pass.
3. Regression test added to tests/r002_leased_claims.rs covering leased-claim -> release -> plain-claim -> close; cargo test passes.
issue.title: Stop lease history from permanently bricking mutation of re-claimed issues

issue.close_reason: Shipped in e803404. Publication serializes on an exclusive flock at .beads/checkpoint/publish.lock, held across object writes, pointer replacement, and tombstone application -- a file lock distinct from the SQLite write path, so mutations commit while a publisher holds it (verified by an integration test that reads the issue back through a second process before releasing). The post-commit chokepoint rechecks coverage under the lock: a worker queued behind the winner rereads the pointer, sees a sequence at or beyond its own, and exits 0 having written nothing (forged-pointer race test). issue.description: SqliteStore::with_path (store/sqlite.rs:57) opens a connection and never calls apply_migrations; only init does (sqlite.rs:325). A workspace created under an older schema therefore never advances, even under a binary whose CURRENT_VERSION is higher. Observed 2026-09-01: 61 of 63 workspaces on ex44 stuck at schema v13 with no attempt_outcomes table (~29k issues). Fix: migrate on open, behind a read-only precheck — apply_migrations unconditionally runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations, so calling it on every open would take a write lock and serialise many workers sharing one workspace. Common path must stay a pure read.
issue.notes: Implementation verified complete. The fix is already in place: open_configured_connection calls migrations::migrate_if_pending, which does a read-only schema_is_current check first (SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_migrations), only applying migrations when the schema is outdated. This keeps the common path (already at CURRENT_VERSION) as a pure read operation, avoiding write lock serialization. All tests pass: migrate_if_pending_advances_a_legacy_store, migrate_if_pending_is_a_noop_when_current, migrate_if_pending_bootstraps_an_unversioned_store. The implementation correctly addresses the reported issue where 61 of 63 workspaces were stuck at schema v13 with no attempt_outcomes table.

issue.description:
src/service/leases.rs:167-178: renew_lease executes 'UPDATE leases SET assignee = ?1, fencing_token = ?2, expires_at = ?3, renewed_at = ?4 WHERE issue_id = ?5' — no assignee predicate. Because create_lease (leases.rs:89-100) INSERTs a fresh row for every leased claim and nothing ever deletes rows, an issue accumulates multiple lease rows over its life; one renewal then rewrites EVERY row for the issue, stamping them all with the renewer's assignee/token/expiry and destroying the per-row lease history the fencing model (monotonic tokens, R002) relies on for auditability.

Fix: constrain the UPDATE with 'AND assignee = ?' (and preferably target only the active row, e.g. the row with MAX(fencing_token) or expires_at > now), and decide/document whether repeated claims should keep inserting new rows or reuse one row per issue.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Integration/unit test that produces two lease rows for one issue (leased claim -> release -> leased claim by another assignee, using the post-beadrs-122d91fb behavior), renews one lease, and asserts the other row's assignee/fencing_token/expires_at are unchanged.
2. Existing tests/r002_leased_claims.rs passes.
3. cargo test passes.

Note: blocked by beadrs-122d91fb because both change src/service/leases.rs and the chosen fix there (e.g. purging rows on release/close) changes what this bead must assert.

issue.description:
Automatic flush must be a no-op when the covered sequence already equals the live event sequence, so a no-op mutation publishes no generation and creates no object.

This rule is only sound once every semantic mutation advances the sequence, which is why it depends on the event work.

Acceptance:
- a mutation that changes nothing publishes no new generation
- a real mutation publishes exactly one generation covering its own sequence
- sync flush-only against a clean checkpoint publishes nothing and exits 0

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 3 and 8; ADR-003.
issue.notes: Implemented plan 6.2.1 items 3 and 8. Chokepoint (src/main.rs publish_after_commit) now skips publication when read_covered_event_sequence(current.json) >= live sequence after dispatch, on top of the existing sequence-advance trigger; >= rather than == also treats a lost publication race as success per item 4's spirit. New read_covered_event_sequence in src/service/checkpoint.rs reads the same authoritative snapshot_sequence field sync --status reports. sync flush-only is idempotent: clean + ready-to-commit checkpoint publishes nothing, prints 'Checkpoint already current', exits 0; the skip is bounded by readiness so a not-ready checkpoint (unresolved tombstones) still republishes and reapplies cleanup. Four new tests in tests/post_commit_publication.rs cover all three acceptance criteria plus the tombstone bound. test_f017_identical_flushes_reuse_one_object pinned the superseded clean-reflush-republishes behavior; updated to trigger republication via a lost pointer (realistic interrupted-publication state) preserving all object-reuse assertions. fmt, clippy, full cargo test suite green. Shipped in 2b1c534.

The double-claim path itself had already been removed by 6662c31; this change completes the fix by building the --why trace from a pre-claim eligibility snapshot (collect_eligibility_factors + build_decision_trace) so selected_factors and the eligibility summary describe decision-time state instead of contradicting the selection. issue.description:
src/main.rs:157-163: cmd_claim calls service::claim_issue_with_trace AFTER the real claim (main.rs:121-154) inside the same committed transaction, and claim_issue_with_trace (src/service/claim.rs:673-696) performs a full claim_issue mutation. So 'bead claim --why' claims TWO beads and silently discards the second ID.

Reproduced live at HEAD (dac3910): fresh workspace, 3 ready beads, one 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why' left TWO beads in_progress assigned to w1. Also the JSON output is self-contradictory: decision_trace.selected_issue_id names the second (hidden) bead while claim_result.bead_id names the first, and selected_factors reports the bead as in_progress/ineligible because the trace is computed after the mutation.

Fix: never invoke the mutating claim path a second time; compute the trace with the read-only create_decision_trace (claim.rs:577) against the bead the first claim actually selected, before/without mutating again. Applies to both FIFO and --policy paths.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. Fresh temp workspace, >=2 ready beads; 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why' then 'bead list --status in_progress --json' shows exactly ONE issue.
2. In 'bead claim --assignee w1 --why --json', decision_trace.selected_issue_id == claim_result.bead_id.
3. Regression test added (tests/r001_decision_traces.rs or tests/cli_claim.rs) asserting single-claim under --why; cargo test passes.
issue.notes: Found at dispatch time that the hidden second claim was already gone at HEAD: 6662c31 (beadrs-b412cc80, landed 2026-08-20) replaced cmd_claim's claim_issue_with_trace call with the read-only create_decision_trace, so criteria 1 (exactly one in_progress) and 2 (selected_issue_id == claim_result.bead_id) already passed. What remained was the other half of the reproduced bug: the trace was assembled from post-mutation state, so selected_factors reported the just-claimed bead as in_progress/assigned/ineligible and the eligibility summary counted it under already_assigned/not_open_status. Fixed in 3f720bb: split create_decision_trace into public read-only collect_eligibility_factors + new build_decision_trace(factors, selected, assignee); cmd_claim (FIFO and --policy paths) now snapshots factors before the claim and assembles the trace afterwards against the bead actually selected; claim_issue_with_trace snapshots the same way. Regression test test_claim_with_why_claims_exactly_one_issue added in tests/r001_decision_traces.rs. Verified live on both paths (fifo-v1 and aging-v1): one in_progress, IDs match, selected_factors shows open/unassigned/eligible. cargo fmt clean, clippy clean, full cargo test 38/38 binaries ok.
issue.title: Fix 'bead claim --why' performing a second hidden claim in cmd_claim

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-0d0cb036. Blocked by the claim-epoch contract child.

Problem:
A recovery worker needs to return abandoned work to the ready frontier, but an unconditional release can target a claim that changed between observation and mutation. A generic force path would recreate the incident by allowing an old reaper observation to release a newer worker.

Scope:
- Add a native compare-and-reap service and CLI operation for automation.
- Require the observed claim-epoch credential and perform eligibility check plus release in one IMMEDIATE transaction.
- For leased claims, normal automated reaping succeeds only when that exact current lease is expired. For explicit operator recovery, require an actor/reason and record a distinct audited override.
- If the issue is no longer in_progress, the assignee changed, the epoch changed, or the lease was renewed, return a machine-readable conflict/no-op and preserve the current owner.
- On success, clear assignment and lease ownership, release resource locks, update revision/events/change feed, and publish a consistent checkpoint.

Acceptance:
- Reaper observes A epoch 1; B becomes current epoch 2 before reap commits; reap of epoch 1 conflicts and B is unchanged.
- Reap of an expired current epoch succeeds exactly once; replay is idempotent or a documented no-op.
- Renewed/unexpired leases cannot be reaped by the automated path.
- Explicit operator recovery is reason-bearing and audit-visible.
- Separate-process concurrency and crash-boundary tests cover the command and service surfaces.
- JSON schema, capabilities, CLI help, and NEEDLE contract documentation expose feature detection and stable reason codes.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Add atomic compare-and-reap recovery for expired claim epochs

Design: execute_command now wraps the full command dispatch in one shared
publication chokepoint (plan 6.2.1 items 1-2, ADR-003 step A1). It
snapshots the live event sequence before dispatch; after the command
returns Ok — strictly after its transaction committed, never inside it —
it publishes a forensic checkpoint generation through the same path
sync flush-only takes, iff the sequence advanced this invocation. No
command classification exists anywhere: the P3 contract
(mutating_command_event_contract.rs) forces every mutating command to
append an audit event, and that event is the publication trigger, so
read-only / no-op / failed commands publish nothing by construction and
a newly added mutating command inherits publication with zero wiring
(acceptance criterion 4 satisfied in the strongest sense).

13 requires the flip to ship with the documentation reversal
(beadrs-db5c099d) at the activation gate. AUTO_FLUSH_COMPILED_DEFAULT
stays false; a workspace opts in per-workspace with
"checkpoint": { "auto_flush": true } in .beads/config.json (explicit
bool wins over the compiled default, so the same key becomes the
post-flip suppressor). This is the exact capability shape sibling bead
beadrs-0ba8668a describes ("auto_flush present once the default flips,
absent before").

Handoff to downstream beads (all blocked on this one):
- beadrs-3ab387b2 (skip-when-clean): publish_after_commit already
  returns early when sequence_after <= sequence_before; add the

issue.description:
Every mutating command in main.rs independently discovers the workspace, opens its own rusqlite connection, commits, and prints. There is no shared path a publication step could hook.

Introduce one shared post-commit chokepoint so every present and future mutating command inherits identical publication behavior, rather than editing ~20 call sites. Publication runs after the transaction commits, never inside it, so a publication failure cannot roll back committed work. Read-only commands never publish.

Acceptance:
- one chokepoint, exercised by all mutating commands
- publication is strictly after commit
- read-only commands do not publish
- adding a mutating command inherits publication without touching its call site

Refs: plan 6.2.1 items 1-2; ADR-003.
issue.title: Add a single post-commit checkpoint publication chokepoint

issue.description:
Where a command rejects an argument a competent operator would expect to work, state the domain rule and the remedy instead of surfacing a bare parser error. Generalizes the standard `release` already sets when it refuses an assigned open issue with "use 'update --clear-assignee' instead".

Verified against the shipped CLI 2026-08-16:

  bead update <id> --title "x"  -> error: unexpected argument '--title' found
                                   tip: to pass '--title' as a value, use '-- --title'
  bead close <id> --body "x"    -> error: unexpected argument '--body' found
                                   tip: to pass '--body' as a value, use '-- --body'

Both are actively misleading: the tip proposes escaping the flag as a positional value, which is never the intent and produces a second confusing failure if followed. Neither states the actual rule. Both are load-bearing enough that downstream environment documentation carries explicit warnings about them.

No currently-rejected invocation becomes accepted. No semantics change. This is message quality only.

Acceptance:
- fields immutable after create (title, description, priority, issue-type) produce an error naming the rule and any supported alternative, e.g. label add|remove for labels
- close --body names --reason
- near-miss handling is bounded to flags that exist on sibling commands, not general fuzzy matching
- conformance scenarios assert the remedy text, not merely a nonzero exit, so the affordance cannot regress to a parser default

Refs: ADR-007; plan section 5 command and process contract; plan section 12 R037.
issue.title: R037: Command errors that name the remedy

issue.description: read_all_attempt_outcomes (service/checkpoint.rs:7449) issues an unguarded SELECT ... FROM attempt_outcomes from publish_forensic_checkpoint_holding (:5799). doctor deliberately tolerates the table's absence ('Attempt outcomes table not present (legacy workspace)') and reports the store healthy, so a v13 workspace passes every diagnostic while checkpoint publication fails on every mutation — the mutation commits to SQLite and the git-tracked checkpoint silently freezes. doctor and the publisher must agree the table is optional. Fix: return an empty set when the table is absent.
issue.title: Publisher must tolerate a legacy workspace without attempt_outcomes

Write scripts/build-from-archive.sh — the only sanctioned way to build a pinned bead-rs binary. The shared NEEDLE checkout (/home/coding/bead-rs, ADR-015) must never be stashed, reset, or checked out to build an older commit.

Behavior:
- Usage: scripts/build-from-archive.sh <sha> [--features <feat,...>]
- Extract: git archive <sha> | tar -x -C <scratch>, with <scratch>=$(mktemp -d -p ~/scratch)
- Build there with CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointing under the same scratch dir
- Copy the built binary to the pinned location (pinned-binaries/) plus a metadata file recording the source sha, binary sha256, features, and build date
- Remove the scratch dir on success; leave it in place on failure for diagnosis (workspace disposable-checkout rule)

Acceptance:
- Running the script for a valid SHA exits 0 and produces the binary + metadata without touching the shared checkout's index, HEAD, or stashes
- A failing build exits nonzero and leaves the scratch dir in place
issue.notes: Shipped scripts/build-from-archive.sh (commit 9e7745c, pushed to origin main): git archive <sha> | tar -x into a fresh mktemp dir under ~/scratch, build there with CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the same dir, install the release binary + <name>.metadata.json (source sha, sha256, features, build date, host, scratch path, build command) to pinned-binaries/ by default (--out to redirect), rm -rf the scratch dir on success, keep it (with build.log) on any failure. Every git call in the script is read-only (rev-parse/show/archive): HEAD, index, reflog and stashes are never touched. Extra flags beyond the spec: --name (pins are <role>-<shaslice>; default bead-<short>), --out (staging; used by the sibling test), refuse-to-overwrite, disk-floor check on ~/scratch, --locked build. issue.description:
src/service/lifecycle.rs: update_issue (14-77), release_issue (80-111), close_issue (114-151), reopen_issue (154-185) all read the issue via get_issue_for_update and validate the --if-revision guard BEFORE starting the write transaction (conn.unchecked_transaction() at lines 65, 106, 146, 180), and the subsequent UPDATE statements match on 'WHERE id = ?' only, with no revision predicate (lines 319, 354, 416, 450 — each does revision = revision + 1 unconditionally).

TOCTOU: a concurrent process (multi-worker shared workspace is the supported model) can commit a change between the pre-transaction read and the write; the guard then passes against the stale revision and the update silently overwrites newer state — exactly the lost update README lines 128-130 promises fails with exit 4. The window is real for separate-process SQLite WAL connections; unchecked_transaction is deferred, so no write lock is held during validation.

Fix: perform the read + revision/lease validation INSIDE the transaction (and take it immediate so the snapshot cannot go stale before the write), or make each UPDATE conditional ('WHERE id = ? AND revision = ?') and map 0 affected rows to the existing conflict/exit-4 path.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. New test with two connections to one workspace: conn A reads revision N; conn B performs an update (revision becomes N+1); conn A then runs a lifecycle op with --if-revision N and MUST get the conflict error (exit 4 semantics), not success.
2. Existing tests/r003_revision_guards.rs passes unchanged.
3. cargo test passes.
issue.notes: Fixed and shipped in 8492103. All four lifecycle ops now take the write transaction IMMEDIATE before reading the issue and validate the revision precondition + lease inside it; every UPDATE carries AND revision = ? with zero-rows-affected mapped to the existing Conflict/exit-4 path. New tests/r003_revision_guard_atomicity.rs (6 tests): a committed competing change makes each op at a stale --if-revision conflict with exit-4 semantics (incl. through the CLI), and the discriminating test races an uncommitted in-flight writer -- the guard waits for the write lock, re-reads, conflicts; the concurrent change survives untouched. Verification notes: (1) full cargo test run has 3 failures in cli_doctor (test_doctor_reports_open_issue_held_by_assignee, test_ready_frontier_emits_r001_reason_codes) and f017_forensic (test_f017_monolithic_checkpoint_basic) -- all three reproduce on pristine HEAD with this change stashed, i.e. pre-existing from the R035 commit ed4fb3d: the doctor message text drifted from what the tests assert ('Ready frontier warning'/'--clear-assignee' expected; doctor emits 'WARN ready_frontier: N open issue(s) are assigned and excluded...' with the remedy only in JSON details). issue.description:
create --unique-ref NAMESPACE:KEY binds an R011 external reference inside the insert transaction; when the reference is already bound, the command returns the existing bead's identity instead of creating a duplicate. The closed-bead case must be explicit (distinct output or flagged conflict) so automation cannot loop on finished work.

Prevents duplicate beads at the source when dispatchers materialize work from the same external identifier concurrently.

Acceptance:
- ref binding and duplicate detection occur in one insert transaction
- ref-hit returns the existing ID with output distinguishable from a fresh create
- closed-bead ref-hit semantics explicit and tested
- concurrent duplicate-create race test: exactly one bead exists afterwards

Refs: plan section 12 R032; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 5 dossier.
issue.notes:
ADR-008 (2026-08-16) records that title-similarity duplicate detection was
considered and REJECTED, and routes duplicate prevention here.

Rationale: ADR-001 already settled that this project does not infer from issue
titles "under any circumstance", and a soft warning is not a weaker commitment —
it still needs a similarity function and threshold, and still fires on sibling
beads, which are normal in this domain. R032's transactional unique-ref is the
only mechanism that can actually guarantee non-duplication.

Consequence for this bead: R032 is now the sole sanctioned answer to "how do I
stop duplicate beads", so its closed-bead case matters more than the plan text
implies. Anyone asking for fuzzy duplicate detection should be directed here.

issue.notes:
Found by beadrs-146944d1 (NEEDLE fallback/atomic validation across pinned variants).

SYMPTOM: bead resolve <id> --attempt-id A --outcome verified_success --action close fails on every workspace, including one the same binary just init'd. Exit code 5, stderr: 'Error: Integrity error: Failed to read issue: SQLite error: no such column: updated_at_revision in SELECT updated_at_revision, base_status, attempt_tier, consecutive_failures FROM issues WHERE id = ?1'. Verified against pinned feature-enabled binary bead-attempt-resolution-f25ab5c (bead 0.2.6, f25ab5c) in a fresh scratch workspace; source inspection shows committed HEAD carries the identical SELECT (src/service/attempt.rs get_issue_state) and no 'updated_at_revision' column exists anywhere in src/store — migrations add 'revision' (migrations.rs:376) and attempt_tier/consecutive_failures (563-567) but never updated_at_revision. IssueState.revision strongly suggests the SELECT meant 'revision'.

BLAST RADIUS: the entire resolve execution path — replay detection, revision guard, fencing token, receipts — is unreachable at runtime, while 'bead capabilities' advertises attempt_outcome.supported=true. A consumer that trusts the advertisement (e.g. NEEDLE) gets a deterministic exit-5 on every resolve. Existing attempt tests never catch it: attempt_outcome_round_trip.rs inserts outcome rows directly into SQLite and never drives get_issue_state.

CONTAINMENT: the failure is atomic — bead state is unchanged after the failed resolve (still Open, revision 1) — and the core dispatch loop (claim/update/close/reopen/release, fencing) is unaffected on both variants. Cross-variant workspaces unaffected.

FIX HINT: select 'revision' (the column migrations actually create) or add the missing migration; add a CLI-driven resolve end-to-end test so the path is exercised for real. tests/needle_variant_dispatch_paths.rs::resolve_execution_fails_with_recorded_integrity_defect_on_feature_enabled_pin regression-pins the current failure mode and must be flipped when this is fixed. Full evidence: docs/verification/needle-variant-dispatch-validation.md (committed with beadrs-146944d1).
issue.title: bead resolve selects nonexistent column updated_at_revision: every resolve exits 5 with an integrity error

issue.description:
'Ready to commit' (src/main.rs:2120) is computed purely from checkpoint internals -- generation alignment, verified root, view agreement, tombstones. It says nothing about whether git can actually reach any of it. bead-rs shells out to git nowhere in src/, so the readiness answer is structurally unable to consider the one thing the phrase implies.

Observed live 2026-09-02 in the commitgraph workspace. Immediately after a flush:

  bead sync status  ->  Dirty: no / Root: objects/2ab05eb7... (verified) / Ready to commit: yes
  git status        ->   M .beads/checkpoint/current.json
                          M .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl
                          M .beads/checkpoint/previous.json
                          ?? .beads/checkpoint/objects/

The checkpoint was consistent and entirely absent from git. That is not a corner case: no commit in that repo carried .beads between 7d584c2 and 2026-09-02, so every bead created in that window existed on exactly one machine. Git is the handoff channel between workers that share no filesystem, so a checkpoint that never reaches it is a durability illusion, and today nothing reports the gap.

Add a git reachability line -- tracked / staged / committed, and which files are unstaged or untracked -- so 'ready to commit' means ready AND not yet done rather than only the former. Read-only; no index or history mutation.

This is bead-rs's first git dependency, so the mechanism is a real choice: shelling out to a git binary versus a Rust implementation (gix / git2). Shelling out is simpler and matches how the checkpoint is consumed in practice; a library avoids depending on git being on PATH. issue.description:
## Source

NEEDLE GitHub issue #16 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/16): a new user
cannot complete the NEEDLE quickstart because there is no install path for a bead
backend. NEEDLE's install.sh will install `bead` from this repo's GitHub release, and
needs a stable asset contract to do it.

## Problem

`declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/bead-rs-ci-workflowtemplate.yml` builds
`target/release/bead` and uploads it as a single bare asset named `bead` (see v0.2.1:
`gh release view v0.2.1 --repo jedarden/bead-rs --json assets`). No architecture in
the name, no `checksums.txt`. An installer cannot select an asset by host arch or
verify what it downloaded.

## Deliverable

Edit the WorkflowTemplate in declarative-config (never kubectl; commit to main, push
to Forgejo origin, ArgoCD app `argo-workflows-ns-iad-ci` syncs it):

- Upload the binary as `bead-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (copy of target/release/bead).
- Generate `checksums.txt` in `sha256sum` format (`<64 hex>  <filename>`, two spaces),
  one line per uploaded executable, and upload it in the same `gh release create`.
- Validate before publishing: checksums.txt non-empty, one entry per asset, every line
  well-formed. Mirror the validation block in `needle-workflowtemplate.yml`
  (~lines 376-445) rather than inventing a new one.
- Keep the existing tag-to-Forgejo and draft-publish logic untouched.
- Do NOT add aarch64 in this bead.

## Definition of done

- The next bead-rs release (bump VERSION, let CI run) shows assets
  `bead-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `checksums.txt` and is not a draft.
- `sha256sum -c checksums.txt` passes against the downloaded binary.
- Close reason names the release tag and the declarative-config commit.

## Notes

Asset contract consumed by: bead-rs install.sh bead (this workspace) and NEEDLE
workspace beads for install.sh (see NEEDLE umbrella for GitHub #16).
issue.notes: Consumers: NEEDLE workspace needle-6de75655 (verification gate), needle-b85c2d42 (install.sh installs bead), umbrella needle-f34f5024 for GitHub jedarden/NEEDLE#16.

issue.description:
Split child 2 of 4 of beadrs-0d3c14c2; blocked by beadrs-7c7a51d4 (SHA verified). This is the mechanical unblocker for the parent's push acceptance: local main and origin/main were diverged (ahead ~100 / behind ~99) at split time, so a plain push is rejected and the record commit cannot land. This divergence is the most likely cause of the parent's five prior failures.

Steps:
1. If `git status -sb` shows no divergence (ahead 0 / behind 0), close immediately with the observed counts - someone else reconciled; do not merge anything.
2. Never force-push, never rebase, never reset. `git pull --no-rebase` (merge commit) or `git merge origin/main`. History note: origin/main carries a force-pushed twin lineage of local main - trees are near-identical, so expect a clean merge and EMPTY tree diffs for twin commits; diff trees, not commit counts.
3. If conflicts appear only under .beads/ (checkpoint artifacts), do NOT hand-craft resolutions: `git merge --abort`, record the conflict list in notes, leave the bead open with the abort reason. Nothing under .beads/ is ever hand-edited.
4. After a clean merge: `git push origin main`, then confirm `git status -sb` reads ahead 0 / behind 0 and `git rev-parse origin/main` == HEAD.
5. Record the merge commit SHA and post-merge ahead/behind in notes.

Acceptance:
- git status -sb shows main in sync with origin/main (0/0) at close
- No force-push, no rebase, no reset attributable to this bead in the reflog
- Merge commit SHA recorded in notes; no source files staged beyond the merge's own resolution

Coordination: beadrs-0d6095d0 (tree-restore, open) may concurrently reconcile state - re-check divergence before merging; if it lands first, close per step 1.
issue.notes:
BLOCKED at push by the Forgejo pre-receive security gate — divergence was NOT the live blocker. State found on dispatch: local main was already reconciled by a prior attempt at 15:20 EDT via merge commit 7d085772f703c253c1bc956c6d595b84699796bb (parents 753b519 local + 63c2ee8 origin; merge tree is IDENTICAL to the local parent tree — clean twin-lineage reconciliation, zero conflicts, nothing extra staged). Verified ahead 101 / behind 0 against a current fetch.

`git push origin main` (plain fast-forward, no force) was REJECTED by the pre-receive hook: "push exceeds the synchronous security-scan budget. New blob bytes: 530272624; limit: 268435456."

Root cause: 467.1 MB of the 505.7 MB novel blob bytes are .beads/traces/<id>/stdout.txt|stderr.txt worker logs. They were added to history by commits acd165d, 154e3d3 and dab6e9d in the unpushed range, then untracked again by 50cd533 ("chore: stop tracking NEEDLE execution traces", which added **/.beads/traces/ to .gitignore) — but untracking does not remove the blobs from history, so ANY push of this tip still carries them.

This cannot be worked around client-side:
- Hook check 3 (tools/forgejo-secret-scan/pre-receive line 150) rejects newly-added .beads/traces/* paths outright, independent of size — so even chunked pushes under 256 MiB would be rejected.
- tools/forgejo-secret-scan/README.md ("Large imports and history rewrites") routes oversized/history-burden pushes to an OPERATOR procedure: fresh bare mirror, git-filter-repo sensitive-data removal, fully-redacted gitleaks scan with zero findings, temporary exact-target guard, authorized mirror push — and states "This exception is an operator procedure, not a pusher-controlled bypass."

Supersedes the parent's five-failure hypothesis (divergence): the actual gate is the pre-receive scan budget + forbidden-path rule. issue.description:
Cargo.toml version was last changed on 2026-08-13 (85f36ac, 'prepare v0.1.3'). Since then main has landed at least two changes to documented, operator-visible behavior, and both still report 'bead 0.1.3':

  1311c3b 2026-08-21  post-commit checkpoint publication chokepoint (R026 auto-flush)
  10e36f5 2026-08-24  clear assignee on reopen to prevent silent ready-frontier exclusion

plus R028 fork identity (acd165d), a dedicated checkpoint file lock (e803404),
and an MSRV raise (d0f7f1e).

CONSEQUENCE
There is no way to tell from 'bead --version' whether a given binary has the
behavior the docs describe. Two binaries eleven days and five behavioral
commits apart are indistinguishable at the CLI.

OBSERVED
On ex44, /home/coding/.cargo/bin/bead (built 2026-08-17 20:36) reports 0.1.3.
Its reopen retains the assignee and it does not auto-publish the checkpoint --
correct for that build, and directly contradicting the environment
documentation, which describes post-08-21 behavior. An operator comparing
'bead --version' against the docs concludes the DOCS are wrong. That is the
actual failure: the version string invited a false bug report against correct
documentation.

SCOPE
Make the reported version distinguish builds. Options, in rough order of
preference:
- Bump the version whenever behavior changes (the changes above are not
  patch-invisible; R026 and the reopen fix each alter what an operator
  observes).
- Embed the git describe / short SHA and build date in --version, so a
  development build is self-identifying between releases.
- At minimum, have --version state that it is a development build when the
  working tree is ahead of the last release tag.

NOTE
This is release hygiene, not a logic error, which is why nothing catches it.
Filed after it produced a real false alarm rather than as a hypothetical.
issue.notes:
RESOLVED: The fix was implemented on 2026-08-26 in commit fcbe257 (just one day after this bead was filed). The build.rs script now embeds:

- Short commit SHA (e.g., '133a457')
- Build timestamp in UTC (e.g., '2026-08-26T12:32:34Z')
- Dirty-tree marker when there are uncommitted tracked changes

The installed binary on ex44 (/home/coding/.cargo/bin/bead) built on 2026-08-26T08:35:50 now reports:
  bead 0.2.1 (133a457 2026-08-26T12:32:34Z)

This fully addresses the bead's requirements. Builds are now self-identifying, with commit SHA and build timestamp clearly distinguishing binaries that differ in documented behavior. The dirty flag also identifies builds from uncommitted trees.

The implementation followed the bead's second preferred option: embedding git describe / short SHA and build date. Version was also bumped to 0.2.1 as the first preferred option suggested.

issue.description:
## Source

NEEDLE GitHub issue #16. The reporter could not find any public install path for
`bead`.

## Problem

README "Install" offers only `cargo install --path .` — requires a clone and Rust
1.85+. There is no binary install path and no one-liner. Footgun: `cargo install bead`
from crates.io installs an UNRELATED crate (an OCI container runtime named `bead`);
`bead-rs` is not on crates.io at all. Nothing in the README warns about this.

## Deliverable

1. `install.sh` at the repo root, modelled on NEEDLE's `install.sh`:
   - resolve the latest release via the GitHub API (fetch the whole JSON into a
     variable first — see NEEDLE's curl broken-pipe note in its install.sh),
   - map `uname -m`/`uname -s` to `<arch>-<os>`, download `bead-<arch>-<os>`,
   - verify against `checksums.txt`, fail closed; explicit `--skip-checksum` /
     `BEAD_SKIP_CHECKSUM=1` opt-out only,
   - install to `~/.local/bin/bead` (override `BEAD_INSTALL_PATH`), idempotent,
   - print a PATH hint if the install dir is not on PATH,
   - `--help`.
2. bead-rs-ci uploads `install.sh` with each release and includes it in checksums.txt
   (declarative-config template edit; depends on the asset-contract bead).
3. README Install section, in this order:
   - `curl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/bead-rs/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash`
   - `cargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/bead-rs --bin bead` (Rust 1.85+)
   - `cargo install --path .` (from a clone)
   - an explicit warning that `cargo install bead` is a different, unrelated crate.
4. Shell tests for the arch map and the checksum failure path (shellcheck clean).

## Definition of done

- In a container with no Rust toolchain, the one-liner installs `bead` and
  `bead --version` prints the release version.
- A tampered checksum aborts the install with a nonzero exit.
- README updated as above; `install.sh` present in the latest release's assets.

issue.description:
Context: NEEDLE ADR-022 (docs/adr/022-…) and Phase 19 §19.2 of NEEDLE's plan. NEEDLE will stop setting `--status blocked`, but a human-set block must still be visible, and NEEDLE's migration (needle-e0e11ed8) needs to enumerate blocked beads without calling `bead why --id` per bead.

## Observed (2026-08-29)
`manual_blocked` is an overlay: `bead list --json`, `bead show`, and `bead doctor ready_frontier` all report such a bead as plain `open`; only `bead why --id` prints `Manual Blocked: true`. `bead list --status blocked` is rejected ("Unknown status: blocked"). 171 open beads across 13 workspaces carried the flag invisibly; warden and sun-sim were fully starved with no visible cause.

## Task

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-0d0cb036.

Problem:
Atomic selection prevents two simultaneous claim winners, but the ownership epoch is not mandatory on later lifecycle mutations. In particular, validate_lease_for_mutation accepts an omitted token when an active lease exists, and ordinary non-leased claims have no durable epoch credential. A process from an older claim can therefore mutate a newer claim after release and reassignment.

Scope:
- Give every successful claim a monotonically increasing, machine-readable claim-epoch credential, for leased and non-leased claims. The existing fencing token may be evolved to serve this role if its renewal semantics remain safe and documented.
- Return the credential from claim/show or a dedicated claim projection so automated consumers can retain it without a second ambiguous lookup.
- Require the exact current credential for claimant-owned update, release, close, reopen, resource-lock changes, and atomic attempt resolve while an issue is claimed. Missing and stale credentials must conflict with exit code 4 and change nothing.
- Preserve manual/operator recovery only through an explicit reason-bearing override that emits a distinct audit/change-feed event. Do not let omission silently mean override.
- Keep validation and mutation in the same IMMEDIATE transaction, including audit, resource locks, attempt receipts, and checkpoint-visible state.

Acceptance:
- Deterministic two-connection test: A claims epoch 1; an explicit recovery releases epoch 1; B claims epoch 2; every A update/release/close/reopen/resolve attempt with epoch 1 conflicts and B remains assigned in_progress.
- The same operations with B epoch 2 succeed.
- Omitting the credential on a claimed issue conflicts unless the explicit audited operator override is used.
- Both leased and non-leased claims are protected; historical lease rows never brick a later valid epoch.
- Twenty-way simultaneous claim coverage still produces one successful claimant per issue.
- Help, JSON/schema, capabilities, audit documentation, and research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md describe the contract.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.

issue.description:
check_dependency_graph() in src/service/doctor.rs queries:

  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT blocked_id) FROM dependencies

The dependencies table has no blocked_id column -- it is blocked_issue_id
(blocked_issue_id, blocker_issue_id, kind, condition). The query therefore
fails to prepare on every invocation, and the surrounding .unwrap_or(0)
swallows the error, so the diagnostic line reports '0 blocked issues'
unconditionally, in every workspace, regardless of the real value.

REPRODUCTION (tradegraph workspace, 454 dependency rows):
  $ bead doctor
    OK dependency_graph: Dependency graph OK: 454 dependencies, 0 blocked issues, no cycles
  $ sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT blocked_id) FROM dependencies'
    Error: no such column: blocked_id
  $ sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT blocked_issue_id) FROM dependencies'
    176

'454 dependencies, 0 blocked issues' is internally impossible -- nonzero
dependency rows cannot yield zero distinct blocked ids -- which is what makes
this visible at all.

IMPACT
A health-check line that is silently and permanently zero. An operator reading
'0 blocked issues' next to a nonzero dependency count may conclude nothing is
blocked, which is the opposite of what the store says.

SCOPE
- Correct the column to blocked_issue_id.
- Restrict to kind = 'blocks': the line is labelled 'blocked issues', and
  relates_to edges are informational and do not block.
- Do not swallow the error. This query failing should be loud; .unwrap_or(0)
  on a diagnostic turns a broken check into a passing one.

NOTE
An audit of all 24 SQL literals in doctor.rs against a real store found this
is the only one that fails to prepare. The other .unwrap_or(0) sites are
latent risk of the same class, not currently wrong -- consider them
separately rather than in this fix.
issue.title: doctor reports '0 blocked issues' in every workspace: query names a nonexistent column

issue.close_reason: Shared pragma-configured opener (src/store::open_configured_connection) now used by every main.rs handler (27 sites) and all 7 doctor diagnostic openings; acceptance grep clean, pragma conformance + functional busy-timeout tests added and passing, full suite green on HEAD+change except one failure pre-existing at HEAD (b9cdef9 profile-flag residue, fix already in flight elsewhere). issue.description:
src/store/sqlite.rs:58-75 and src/store/mod.rs:116-131 deliberately configure every store connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL. But ~25 command handlers in src/main.rs open raw rusqlite::Connection::open(&db_path) with NONE of these (lines 109, 271, 308, 379, 443, 488, 517, 552, 600, 622, 651, 726, 777, 808, 833, 873, 918, 1034, 1468, 1619, 2110, 2263, 2356), as do src/service/doctor.rs:451 and 495.

Consequences: (a) SQLite foreign_keys defaults OFF per-connection, so every 'FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE' declared in src/store/migrations.rs (lines 128-412) is unenforced on the CLI's primary code paths; (b) busy_timeout=0 means concurrent fleet access (multiple workers running bead claim/update against one workspace, the tool's core use case) hits immediate SQLITE_BUSY -> exit 1 instead of waiting up to 5s, undermining the concurrent-claim contract documented in README 'Coordinating a fleet'. cmd_claim (main.rs:102-116) also uses unchecked_transaction (deferred) on such a raw connection.

Fix: add one shared helper (e.g. in src/store) that opens + applies the same pragmas as SqliteStore, and use it from every handler in main.rs and doctor.rs; remove direct Connection::open calls there.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. grep -n "Connection::open(" src/main.rs src/service/doctor.rs returns no raw call sites (only the shared helper, or nothing).
2. A test asserts the connection used by a representative handler has foreign_keys=1 and busy_timeout=5000 (query 'PRAGMA foreign_keys; PRAGMA busy_timeout;').
3. cargo test passes.
issue.notes:
Shipped in 4d08718 (pushed to origin/main).

What changed:
- src/store exposes open_configured_connection() -- single pragma configuration point (foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL). SqliteStore internals and workspace discovery now route through it too (discovery previously set only 2 of the 4 pragmas).
- All 27 raw Connection::open sites in main.rs (25 handler sites + the publication-chokepoint helper + the post-restore publication path) and all 7 in doctor.rs now use it. Acceptance grep 'grep -n "Connection::open(" src/main.rs src/service/doctor.rs' returns nothing; the only Connection::open left in src/ is inside the helper itself (plus recurrence.rs test code, out of scope).
- tests/connection_pragmas.rs: asserts foreign_keys=1 / busy_timeout=5000 / journal_mode=wal / synchronous=1 via the PRAGMA queries on the shared opener every handler uses, plus a functional test proving the timeout waits out a held WAL write lock instead of failing immediately.

Acceptance (cargo test): full suite run on HEAD+this-change: 43/44 test binaries green; the one failure (test_sync_flush_only_rejects_invalid_profile, cli_sync) fails identically on pure HEAD -- pre-existing residue of the b9cdef9 --profile removal, whose fix is already in another worker's uncommitted tests/cli_sync.rs. Both new tests pass in the live tree as well.

Finding worth a follow-up (filed as a new bead): SQLite does NOT invoke the busy handler when a DEFERRED transaction that has already read tries to upgrade to a write transaction -- that returns immediate SQLITE_BUSY regardless of busy_timeout. All mutating handlers use unchecked_transaction() (deferred), so handler-vs-handler write contention still fails fast; the pragma fix covers lock-acquisition paths (autocommit writes, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, publication) and foreign_keys enforcement. Converting mutating handlers to BEGIN IMMEDIATE is the separate fix.

Concurrency note: verified and committed while R035/R036 workers had uncommitted edits in the same files; the commit was staged from the exact verified HEAD+change tree so no in-flight foreign work was swept in.

issue.description:
## Summary

`bead update <id> --notes "..."` reports success and bumps the issue revision,
but the note text is not persisted anywhere. It is not in the SQLite store, not
in the checkpoint, and not in `bead show --json` — there is no `notes` field at
all, and `comments` stays empty.

This is silent data loss on a **documented** flag. `bead update --help` lists it
under both EXAMPLES and OPTIONS:

    bead update ID --notes "Investigated root cause"   # Add investigation notes
    --notes <NOTES>    New notes

Version: bead 0.1.3.

## Reproduction (isolated, empty workspace)

    mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro && git init -q .
    bead init --prefix repro
    ID=$(bead create --title repro --priority 3)
    bead update "$ID" --notes "SENTINEL_NOTE_VALUE_12345"; echo "rc=$?"
    bead show "$ID" --json
    grep -r SENTINEL_NOTE_VALUE_12345 .

Observed:

- `rc=0`
- `bead show --json` returns keys: assignee, comments, created_at,
  dependencies, description, id, labels, priority, revision, status, title,
  updated_at. No `notes`. `comments` is `[]`.
- `revision` goes 1 -> 2 and `updated_at` advances, so a mutation WAS committed.
- The sentinel string appears in **no file in the workspace** — not
  `.beads/beads.db`, not `.beads/checkpoint/`.

## Why this is worse than a missing feature

The revision bump is the dangerous part. A caller that writes a note and then
checks 'did my update apply?' sees a changed revision and concludes yes. Any
optimistic-concurrency caller using `--if-revision` also burns a revision for
a write that stored nothing.

This bit in practice while filing declarat-751aca4f in declarative-config: a
correction was attached with `--notes`, appeared to succeed, and was gone.
Because `bead update` also cannot change a description, the only recovery was
to close that bead and recreate it — so the failure mode costs a bead ID and
leaves a spurious closed issue behind.

## Expected

One of, in order of preference:

1. Persist the note — expose it as a `notes` field on the issue and in
   `show --json`, and include it in the checkpoint so it survives a rebuild.
2. Append it as a comment, since `comments` already exists in the schema and is
   the natural home for investigation notes.
3. If `--notes` is genuinely not implemented, make it a hard usage error and
   remove it from `--help`. A flag that exits 0 and does nothing is the worst
   of the three.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reproduction above finds the sentinel after the update, via
  `bead show --json` and in the checkpoint.
- A regression test asserts a note round-trips through
  create -> update --notes -> show, and through a checkpoint flush + rebuild.
- No revision is consumed by an update that stores nothing.
issue.title: update --notes silently discards the note: rc=0, revision bumps, content stored nowhere

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-8c343a7c (claim-epoch fencing umbrella). Child 2 of 5 - turns child 1's credential into a hard fence.

Problem:
validate_lease_for_mutation accepts an omitted token while an active lease exists, and non-leased claims carry no credential at all, so a process holding an older claim can mutate a newer claim after release and reassignment. This is the defect that produced the 2026-09-03 spaxel duplicate-dispatch incident.

Scope:
- Require the exact current claim-epoch credential for claimant-owned mutations while an issue is claimed: update, release, close, reopen, resource-lock add/remove, and atomic attempt resolve.
- Missing and stale credentials must conflict with exit code 4 and change nothing - no partial write, no revision bump, no event.
- Keep credential validation and the mutation in the same IMMEDIATE transaction, including audit events, resource locks, attempt receipts, and checkpoint-visible state.
- Both leased and non-leased claims are protected; historical lease rows never brick a later valid epoch.
- Mutations on unclaimed (open, unassigned) issues keep working without a credential.

Acceptance:
- A claimed issue's update, release, close, reopen, resource-lock change, and resolve without a credential each exit 4 and change nothing (verified by re-read of status, assignee, and revision).
- The same operations carrying a stale credential from a superseded epoch exit 4 and leave the current claim intact.
- The current claimant performing the same operations with the exact current credential succeeds.
- Twenty-way simultaneous claim coverage still yields exactly one successful claimant per issue.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Require the exact claim-epoch credential on claimant-owned mutations

issue.description:
cmd_init returns early on WorkspaceState::Ready, before reaching apply_migrations. Nothing else in the CLI applies a pending migration to an existing store: doctor --repair does not create tables, and no migrate subcommand exists.

CONSEQUENCE
Installing a newer binary over an older store leaves every workspace short of
the tables the new code queries. The failure is deferred to whichever command
touches one first and surfaces as a bare SQLite error that names neither the
schema version nor a remedy:

  $ bead list --ready
  bead: SQLite error: no such table: issue_resource_keys

OBSERVED ON EX44
A binary built 2026-08-17 sat at schema v9 while the current binary expects
v13 (issue_resource_keys arrives in the 10..13 range). Upgrading broke 'bead
list --ready' and 'bead claim' -- the core of the NEEDLE fleet loop -- across
62 of 63 workspaces simultaneously. 'bead doctor' still passed, because it
touches none of the new tables, so the store looked healthy while the frontier
was unreadable.

'bead init' printing 'Workspace already exists' and exiting 0 is what makes
this hard to diagnose: the documented recovery path reports success without
doing anything.

FIX
init applies pending migrations when the workspace is Ready, reporting
'Applied pending migrations: schema N -> M' or 'Schema up to date (version N)'.
Migrations are versioned and idempotent, so this is safe to run unconditionally
and is what the init help text already promises ('Repeated initialization with
the same prefix is safe and deterministic').

Deliberately NOT auto-migrating on every store open: a partial upgrade racing
several live workers is a worse failure than an explicit repair step, and
CLAUDE.md already documents 'bead init' as the schema-rebuild path.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING SEPARATELY
Commands that fail on a missing table could compare the store's
schema_migrations version against CURRENT_VERSION and say 'workspace is at
schema 9, this binary expects 13 -- run bead init' instead of surfacing raw
SQLite text.
issue.notes: Verification completed: Fix is present in src/main.rs lines 438-459. The code correctly applies pending migrations when init finds an existing workspace in Ready state, reporting 'Applied pending migrations: schema N -> M' or 'Schema up to date (version N)'. This was implemented in commit 90708b8 and the bead was closed in commit 1d04fd5.
issue.title: upgrading the binary strands every existing workspace at its old schema

issue.close_reason: Landed in 4a11ea8: flush resolves the mode from .beads/config.json (checkpoint.mode/thresholds), the previous sharded manifest's recorded table, then the plan 6.1.1 defaults (50k records / 64 MiB / 8 MiB line); forced monolith is refused above recorded limits. Sharded publisher retains a valid partition plan, splits only overflowing shards, and seals event/receipt objects so one mutation republishes only the changed shard plus the event tail (verified at 30 vs 300 issues). Mode transitions tombstone the superseded root after the pointer commits; monolithic and sharded restores verified equivalent. Full suite, clippy, and fmt green; tests/checkpoint_mode_selection.rs (9 tests) covers all four acceptance criteria.
issue.description:
main.rs cmd_sync_flush_only hardcodes CheckpointMode::Monolithic, so the sharded publication path in checkpoint.rs is unreachable and every flush re-serializes the whole workspace. Flush is therefore linear in workspace size: 0.01s at 100 issues, 0.03s at 400, 0.07s at 1600.

Plan section 6.1.1 already specifies the thresholds (50,000 issue records, 64 MiB total, 8 MiB per record line) and the prefix-split partition plan, and specifies sealed append-only event tail objects so a frequently updated bead does not rewrite its history-bearing shard. Implement mode selection from the recorded thresholds, retaining an existing valid partition plan and splitting only overflowing shards.

Acceptance:
- mode is selected from recorded configuration/thresholds, not a constant
- crossing a threshold publishes a mode transition whose changed-path set includes the new root, objects, pointer replacement, and tombstones for the superseded root
- publication after one mutation writes bytes proportional to the changed shard plus event tail, demonstrated at two workspace sizes an order of magnitude apart
- monolithic and sharded restores are semantically equivalent

Refs: plan 6.1.1, 6.2.1 P4; ADR-003.
issue.title: Select sharded checkpoint mode from recorded thresholds instead of hardcoding monolithic

issue.description:
## Problem

bead claim has no check for whether the requesting assignee already holds an in_progress issue elsewhere in the same workspace. This lets one assignee accumulate unbounded simultaneous in_progress claims with no upper limit.

Real incident (2026-08-17, commitgraph workspace, a NEEDLE-fleet consumer of bead-rs): one assignee (claude-code-glm-5-commitgraph-2) held 9 simultaneous in_progress beads, another (claude-code-glm-5-adr018) held 8. All 25 in_progress beads in that workspace were confirmed stale (no live process working the repo; last real file touch predated even the freshest claim's updated_at) and released by hand. Ready frontier went 0 -> 22 after release.

## Proposed behavior

Add an opt-in claim-time guard, following the same per-call opt-in pattern leasing already uses (src/service/leases.rs: DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL/MIN_LEASE_TTL/MAX_LEASE_TTL are caller-supplied via the existing --lease-ttl flag on bead claim, not stored workspace config -- this should work the same way, not as a .beads/config.json default).

Proposed flag: bead claim --assignee X --single-claim (name TBD). When set, claim_issue (src/service/claim.rs:130) checks -- within the same transaction, same workspace database, before find_eligible_issue (claim.rs:638) / find_eligible_frontier (claim.rs:829) run -- whether X already has any issue with base status in_progress in this workspace. If so, refuse with a new ReasonCode (e.g. AssigneeHasActiveClaim) naming the blocking issue ID, rather than proceeding to select and assign a new one.

Scoped to this workspace's own database only. bead-rs stores are already one-per-workspace (one beads.db per repo), so this is a same-transaction query against the local issues table -- no cross-workspace lookup is needed or possible, and none is wanted: the point is per-workspace containment, not a global assignee registry.

## What this does and doesn't fix

Bounds impact, does not eliminate staleness. An assignee can still abandon their one claim and let it go stale -- this guard doesn't detect or reap that, it only prevents accumulation. With it, the ceiling is 1 stale claim per assignee per workspace, not unbounded.

Complementary to, not a replacement for:
- needle-d9a36be9 (NEEDLE): mend's own-newer-claim detection heuristic -- backstop for whatever still goes stale within the ceiling of 1
- Adopting the existing --lease-ttl mechanism in NEEDLE's claim path -- bounds how long that 1 stale claim can persist before another worker can reclaim it

## Scope: only the claim action itself

Applies only to the path where claim_issue / claim_issue_with_lease / claim_issue_with_policy newly assigns a previously-unassigned ready issue to an assignee -- i.e. where the assignee relationship is first established by a claim. Does NOT apply to other paths that set an assignee on an issue, e.g. bead update --assignee on an already-open issue. That is a distinct, already-tracked bug shape (NEEDLE bead needle-44e7e5cd: open+assignee issues invisible to the ready frontier, not a real active claim) with different consequences and should not be entangled with this guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New opt-in flag on bead claim (e.g. --single-claim); default behavior unchanged when the flag is omitted
- [ ] With the flag set, claim fails with a distinct, machine-readable reason (new ReasonCode) when the assignee already holds an in_progress issue in this workspace, naming the blocking issue ID
- [ ] The check runs inside the same atomic transaction as selection/assignment -- no race between check and assign
- [ ] Does not alter bead update --assignee behavior on open issues
- [ ] Fixture: assignee holds one in_progress issue; bead claim --single-claim for the same assignee returns AssigneeHasActiveClaim and assigns nothing; after releasing or closing that issue, the same assignee can claim normally again
issue.title: bead claim: refuse a new claim when the assignee already holds an in_progress issue in this workspace

issue.description:
Follow-on to auto-staging. Give the convenience of a correct checkpoint commit without making it implicit: stage the verified set, refuse when the checkpoint is dirty or ahead, and record it with a bead-only pathspec so nothing else in a shared index is swept in.

Automatic committing on every mutation was considered and rejected. Four reasons, each observed rather than hypothesised on 2026-09-02:

1. Pre-commit gates. Checkpoint commits were blocked for hours by a tree-wide Definition of Done gate failing on an unrelated Go regression. An automatic committer must either be hostage to unrelated code health or bypass the gate; bypassing is precisely what lets broken code land.
2. Shared checkouts. Several workers mutate .beads concurrently on one working tree. Committing on every mutation contends for the index lock with agents' own staging, which is the race that swept an unrelated file into commit 780243a in commitgraph.
3. Committing is policy, not storage: branch, detached HEAD, mid-rebase or mid-merge state, authorship and message are all decisions the tool would have to guess, and guessing wrong rewrites shared history.
4. A commit alone does not propagate. Without a push the checkpoint still never leaves the machine, and automatic pushing is a substantially larger hammer.

An explicit subcommand keeps the decision with whoever owns the branch while removing every mechanical way to get the commit wrong.

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-8c343a7c (claim-epoch fencing umbrella). Child 1 of 5 - issuance and visibility only; enforcement lands in later children.

Problem:
Atomic claim selection prevents two simultaneous winners, but an ordinary non-leased claim gives the claimant no durable ownership credential, and leased claims expose a fencing token whose omission is tolerated by later mutations. Without a per-claim credential there is nothing for a fence to require.

Scope:
- Implement a monotonically increasing, machine-readable claim-epoch credential issued on every successful claim, for leased and non-leased claims alike. The existing lease fencing token may be evolved into this role if its renewal semantics remain safe and documented.
- Persist it durably so it survives restart, clone recovery, and checkpoint rebuild (checkpoint-visible state).
- Monotonic per issue: a later claim on the same issue always yields a strictly greater epoch, including after release, reopen, and reclaim.
- Implement the credential in `bead claim` output and in `bead show`/JSON projection (or a dedicated claim projection) so automated consumers can retain it without a second ambiguous lookup.
- Historical lease rows must never brick or collide with a later valid epoch.

Acceptance:
- A claim on a fresh issue returns a credential; the same issue released and reclaimed returns a strictly greater one.
- Leased and non-leased claim paths both carry a credential.
- The credential appears in claim output, show/JSON output, and checkpoint-visible state.
- No enforcement yet in this child: omitting the credential is still accepted by every mutation, and all existing tests keep passing.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.

issue.description:
Discovered while fixing beadrs-98f229c0 (pragma-configured connections, shipped in 4d08718): SQLite does not invoke the busy handler when a connection holding a read snapshot -- a DEFERRED transaction that has already executed a read -- attempts to upgrade to a write transaction. That upgrade returns immediate SQLITE_BUSY regardless of busy_timeout. Reproduced empirically: with one connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE, a second connection in a deferred BEGIN that has run a SELECT fails its next INSERT instantly (0.000s) despite busy_timeout=5000, while a fresh autocommit write on the same connection waits out the lock and succeeds.

Every mutating command path uses rusqlite unchecked_transaction() (deferred): lifecycle.rs (4x), recurrence.rs (3x), external_refs.rs (2x), data.rs (2x), dependencies.rs (5x), checkpoint.rs (several), main.rs cmd_create/cmd_claim. So even with the shared pragma opener in place, two fleet workers running bead claim/update concurrently against one workspace can still hit immediate 'database is locked' -> exit 1 on the read-to-write upgrade, undermining the README 'Coordinating a fleet' concurrency contract that beadrs-98f229c0 was meant to restore.

The one existing counterexample is checkpoint.rs execute_restore_into_empty, which already uses TransactionBehavior::Immediate and documents why: holding the write transaction before inspecting the target prevents races.

Fix: convert the mutating handlers' unchecked_transaction() calls to immediate transactions (Transaction::new_unchecked(conn, TransactionBehavior::Immediate) or unchecked_transaction_with_behavior), starting each write transaction before its first read so lock acquisition happens up front and busy_timeout actually governs contention.

Acceptance:
- a test where two connections (or two CLI invocations) contend on a mutating command demonstrates the loser waits via busy_timeout rather than failing immediately (contrast with the documented pre-fix behavior in tests/connection_pragmas.rs)
- no deferred read-then-write upgrade remains on any mutating command path
- cargo test passes

Care: this changes lock ordering (write lock acquired before reads), which serializes more aggressively and can change deadlock characteristics between multi-transaction commands (e.g. publication chokepoint vs command transaction); review each conversion site for lock scope. Refs: beadrs-98f229c0; tests/connection_pragmas.rs known-limit note.
issue.title: Convert mutating handlers' deferred transactions to BEGIN IMMEDIATE so busy_timeout governs fleet write contention

issue.description:
Report open beads that carry an assignee. Such a bead is not an active claim — a claim sets in_progress — but it IS excluded from the ready frontier, so no worker will ever select it. Advisory only: doctor never clears an assignee, because a parked reservation and abandoned residue are indistinguishable at the schema level and only the operator knows which is which. R034's sibling for the open lifecycle state.

The initial check shipped in 18fa7ee ahead of reason-code convergence and currently emits prose. This bead covers closing that gap, not the initial implementation.

Field evidence 2026-08-16: 583 beads in this state across 47 of 66 workspaces, ten with an entirely empty ready frontier while workers starved and every diagnostic reported clean. Median age 26h, oldest 37h. In one workspace 39 of 40 had zero active blockers — assignment alone held them.

Acceptance:
- emits stable R001-namespace reason codes rather than prose, matching R034's requirement to share semantics rather than invent parallel ones
- machine-readable list of held ids, not ids embedded in a message string
- decide and specify whether an intentionally-held assignment can be declared, so the warning stays meaningful in workspaces that park work on purpose
- doctor still never clears an assignee, including under --repair
- conformance scenario covering healthy -> warning -> cleared

Refs: ADR-005; plan section 7 doctor list; plan section 12 R035; sibling R034 (beadrs-90c9afc9); reason codes R001.
issue.title: R035: Assignment-held readiness diagnosis (doctor ready_frontier)

issue.description:
## Problem

CI runs on Argo Workflows in iad-ci, so GitHub shows no checks, no green tick and no
badge — a reviewer cannot tell that tests run at all. shields.io already serves
`https://img.shields.io/github/checks-status/jedarden/bead-rs/main` from GitHub commit
statuses; it reports "pending" today only because nothing posts a status.

## Precondition (cross-repo, cannot be a blocks edge)

declarative-config bead "github-commit-status: post iad-ci results to GitHub commit
statuses" is merged and `curl -s https://img.shields.io/github/checks-status/jedarden/bead-rs/main.json`
no longer returns "pending" for this repo. If it still does, `bead release` this bead.

## Deliverable

Add to the README badge row:

    [![iad-ci](https://img.shields.io/github/checks-status/jedarden/bead-rs/main?label=iad-ci)](docs/post-push-ci.md or the CI doc this repo has)

Keep existing dynamic badges; remove any hand-typed version badge in the same row.

## Definition of done

- README renders the badge with a real state (passing/failing), not "pending".
- Commit touches README.md only.
issue.notes: Precondition check: shields.io badge still returns 'pending' (verified with curl). The declarative-config bead for posting GitHub commit statuses has not been merged yet, or Argo has not started posting statuses for this repo. Cannot add the badge until it shows a real state (passing/failing).
issue.title: Add the iad-ci status badge to README once Argo posts GitHub commit statuses

issue.description:
Two symptoms, one feature area, both reproducible on main as of 154e3d3+dee7123 (verified with sources stashed to pristine HEAD):

1. tests/r028_fork_identity.rs — 5 failures (8 pass): test_fork_creates_fork_receipt, test_fork_creates_summary_event, test_fork_never_implicit_or_inferred, test_fork_requires_checkpoint, test_fork_requires_clean_checkpoint. In-process calls die with `UNIQUE constraint failed: events.sequence` (the fork summary event reuses a live sequence), and test_fork_requires_checkpoint expects an error that no longer fires.

2. tests/mutating_command_event_contract.rs::every_mutating_command_advances_the_live_event_sequence fails at `bead sync reconcile`: the covered-ahead qualifier "valid staged stream" (src/service/reconcile.rs:216 -> checkpoint.rs:2716 -> validate_event_sequence, checkpoint.rs:2930) demands every origin's first staged event have origin_event_sequence == 1, but an R028 fork origin (e.g. <uuid>-fork-52-<hash>) legitimately starts at the fork point (53). reconcile therefore fails closed on any cloned workspace's checkpoint, while the fork workspace's own publication path accepts the same stream — the two paths disagree.

Design fork to resolve (pick one, record in the R027/R028 specs):
- validate_event_sequence accepts a fork origin starting at its recorded fork point (check against the fork identity, not 1), or
- R028 records origin_event_sequence restarting at 1 per origin, or
- reconcile treats fork-origin streams under a separate qualifier.

Repro: TMPDIR=/var/tmp/<clean> cargo test --no-fail-fast --test r028_fork_identity --test mutating_command_event_contract

Refs: research/specs/remote-advanced-reconcile-v1.md; commit acd165d (R028); commit 154e3d3 (swept the contract-test extension that exposed this). Filed from beadrs-e854d52a (R033) whose full-suite gate surfaced the cluster.
issue.title: R028 fork identity breaks sync reconcile and its own conformance tests
